I'm using this script now to create a sandbox in opencode from my worktrees that are missing

```sh #!/usr/bin/env bash # oc-sync-worktrees.sh — Register all untracked git worktrees with opencode # # Usage: oc-sync-worktrees.sh [/path/to/repo] # Defaults to current directory. set -euo pipefail PROJECT_DIR="$(cd "${1:-.}" && pwd)" DB="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/opencode/opencode.db" if [ ! -f "$DB" ]; then echo "error: opencode database not found at $DB" >&2 exit 1 fi # Find the project row by its worktree path ROW=$(sqlite3 "$DB" "SELECT id, sandboxes FROM project WHERE worktree = '$PROJECT_DIR';") if [ -z "$ROW" ]; then echo "error: no opencode project found for $PROJECT_DIR" >&2 exit 1 fi PROJECT_ID=$(echo "$ROW" | cut -d'|' -f1) SANDBOXES=$(echo "$ROW" | cut -d'|' -f2) # Get all git worktree paths (skip the main worktree) MAIN=$(git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" worktree list --porcelain | head -1 | sed 's/^worktree //') WORKTREES=$(git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" worktree list --porcelain | grep '^worktree ' | sed 's/^worktree //' | grep -v "^${MAIN}$" || true) if [ -z "$WORKTREES" ]; then echo "no secondary worktrees found" exit 0 fi MISSING=() while IFS= read -r wt; do if echo "$SANDBOXES" | grep -q "$wt"; then echo " already registered: $wt" else echo " missing: $wt" MISSING+=("$wt") fi done <<< "$WORKTREES" if [ ${#MISSING[@]} -eq 0 ]; then echo "all worktrees are registered" exit 0 fi # Build updated JSON array NEW="$SANDBOXES" for wt in "${MISSING[@]}"; do if [ "$NEW" = "[]" ]; then NEW="[\"$wt\"]" else NEW="${NEW%]},\"$wt\"]" fi done sqlite3 "$DB" "UPDATE project SET sandboxes = json('$NEW'), time_updated = $(date +%s000) WHERE id = '$PROJECT_ID';" echo "" echo "registered ${#MISSING[@]} worktree(s)" ```

I think I found the culprit (I see it for a lof of other models).
Most LLM providers (like Bedrock) have a TTL (time to live) that is equal to five minutes

Due to the way LLM works, you need to store information about all the previous tokens to predict the next token. That is the concept of a KV cache.

AI providers clean this cache every five minutes. So when you have a long context and you send a new message after five minutes, you will have to redo the computation on all previous tokens.

If you can have access to detailed logs that gives you the cache hit and the price of each request, you will see that most requests have a very low price, but some of them have a huge price because the cache have been cleared.

## Bug

  `opencode auth login` always fails with "Failed to authorize" and token refresh fails
  with `Error: Token refresh failed: 429` even when the authorization code is valid.

  ## Root Cause

  Found in `opencode-anthropic-auth@0.0.13` — the OAuth token exchange and refresh
  requests have two bugs:

  1. **Wrong Content-Type** — sends `application/json` but Anthropic's endpoint requires
     `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` per OAuth 2.0 spec (RFC 6749 §4.1.3)

  2. **Missing User-Agent** — Anthropic's `/v1/oauth/token` endpoint requires
     `User-Agent: claude-cli/2.1.2 (external, cli)`. Requests without it are silently
     rejected with HTTP 429 `rate_limit_error` instead of a proper error message.

  ## Fix

  In `index.mjs`, update both `exchange()` and the refresh block inside `fetch()`:

  ```js
  headers: {
    "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded",
    "User-Agent": "claude-cli/2.1.2 (external, cli)",
  },
  body: new URLSearchParams({ ...params }).toString(),

# opencode-runtime-fallback — model fallback plugin (available today)
For anyone who needs this before it lands natively — I built an OpenCode plugin that implements model fallback: **[opencode-runtime-fallback](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-runtime-fallback)** ([source](https://github.com/youngbinkim0/opencode-fallback))
## Install
```bash
npm install opencode-runtime-fallback
```
## Per-agent fallback chain (`opencode.json`)
```json
{
  "plugin": ["opencode-runtime-fallback"],
  "agent": {
    "coder": {
      "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6",
      "fallback_models": [
        "openai/gpt-5.4",
        "kimi-for-coding/k2p5"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```
## Global config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode-fallback.jsonc`)
Applies to all agents that don't define their own `fallback_models`.
```jsonc
{
  "fallback_models": ["openai/gpt-5.4", "kimi-for-coding/k2p5"], // global chain; optional
  "max_fallback_attempts": 5,    // how many models to try before giving up
  "cooldown_seconds": 60,        // how long a failed model is skipped
  "timeout_seconds": 30,         // abort if no tokens arrive within N seconds (streaming models are never interrupted)
  "retry_on_errors": [429, 500, 502, 503, 504], // HTTP codes that trigger fallback
  "retryable_error_patterns": [], // extra regex patterns matched against error messages
  "notify_on_fallback": true     // show toast when switching models
}
```
## What it does
- Intercepts rate limits, quota errors, model-not-found, and other transient failures and replays the last user message on the next model in the chain
- TTFT timeout — aborts models that produce no tokens within the configured window; models actively streaming are never interrupted
- Cooldown + auto-recovery — failed models sit out for a configurable period, then the plugin switches back to primary automatically
- Per-agent chains override the global chain; the global chain is used for any agent that doesn't define its own
